key_insight: Pretraining on a large CFD dataset helps most when the target problem is close to the source distribution. This paper shows that distribution shifts from geometry changes and added physics can reduce pretraining gains, and quantifies how much each shift component matters.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the open question of why and when pretrained neural PDE surrogates transfer well to new CFD settings, especially when airfoil geometry and turbulence/transition modeling change between source and target data.
method: Pretrain a neural PDE surrogate on 254,909 RANS simulations from one airfoil family.
Fine-tune the model on a new airfoil family under two target regimes: same Spalart-Allmaras (SA) modeling and SA plus e^N transition modeling.
Compare performance under matched freestream ranges to isolate the effect of distribution shift on transfer learning gains.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building physics surrogates, the results clarify when pretraining is worth the effort and when mismatch in geometry or physics can limit transfer. This can guide data collection, model reuse, and fine-tuning strategy in CFD and other scientific ML settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing pretraining on source airfoils and fine-tuning on target airfoils.
Side-by-side comparison of the two target settings: SA vs. SA + e^N transition.
Performance chart illustrating transfer gains under different distribution shifts.
Icon set for geometry shift, physics shift, and data efficiency.
paper_title: How Does Distribution Shift Shape Pretraining Gains in Neural PDE Surrogates?
paper_authors: Pochinapeddi Sai Bhargav, Nithin Somasekharan, Rohit Sunil Kanchi, Sicheng He, Shaowu Pan
